# IX-chain-ORIGINAL-index-language-ACER-SEAT

Public Acer-seat receipt for the original IX index-language/token-savings line.

## Frame

MEASURED_ACER: the public Acer audit clone of `asolaria-behcs-256/data/agent-index` contains a real IX index surface, not a loose note. On 2026-07-05 it measured 425 files, 5 directories, 945,513 bytes, 381 IX-named markdown files, and 31 catalog/chain/cross-reference files. Its catalog reports 484 total entries.

CANON_POINTER: `patterns/IX-060.md` names the core rule: the index is the language. IX numbers are vocabulary, chains are sentences, and `CATALOG.md` is the dictionary. This is the Acer IX counterpart to the Liris LX chain-token-savings line.

MEASURED_PUBLIC_REDUCTIONS: the reductions repo records the growth curve: rich IX/LX index at 224 docs gives 8.38x tuple-meta compression, and the root IX/LX corpus at 1,084 docs gives 38.53x corpus-index compression with an 8-byte-handle floor of 292x.

OPERATOR_PROVIDED_LINEAGE: Jesse described the original one-direction chain sentence shape as `@from [liris] machine [lx 1] time[1-24-2026] ask [ix-1] (acer) tool [eds18] skill [38] run program [1873]`. This repo binds the Acer-side IX evidence to that original LX-chain language idea without claiming that every private local corpus byte is published here.

## Boundary

This repo does not dump hidden `.claude` memory, private local caches, keys, vaults, or full machine snapshots. It publishes a public-safe proof map: counts, hashes, line-oriented evidence pointers, and HBP/HBI receipts.

## Files

- `docs/ACER-IX-ORIGINAL-INDEX-LANGUAGE-2026-07-05.md` - narrative proof map.
- `evidence/acer-ix-census-20260705.csv` - measured Acer IX corpus census.
- `evidence/acer-ix-evidence-pointers-20260705.csv` - path/hash evidence pointers.
- `evidence/acer-ix-source-manifest-20260705.json` - structured manifest.
- `receipts/ACER-IX-ORIGINAL-INDEX-LANGUAGE-2026-07-05.hbp` - HyperBEHCS tuple receipt.
- `receipts/ACER-IX-ORIGINAL-INDEX-LANGUAGE-2026-07-05.hbi` - index receipt.
- `*.sha256` sidecars - byte verification tokens.
